vision.oneLine: The rules of conduct for a chartered accountant: the principles, the CA Act, the two Schedules of misconduct and the Council guidelines.
vision.why:
Ethics is clause recognition under time pressure. Almost every question is a short fact pattern that you must match to the right clause and then give a verdict. The marks are in naming the exact clause, applying each ingredient to a fact, and concluding with the clause again.

It also feeds the rest of AAA: communication with the previous auditor, independence, confidentiality and the audit limits are the ethics side of every audit chapter.

items: (8) to (12): previous auditor, 139 to 141, fees, other business, signing

map.h: Other parts and the Second Schedule
items: Second Schedule Part I: ten duty-of-care clauses
Second Schedule II and III, including SS II(5)
Keep SM figures; add a line on the 2026 Code

sixty: Four layers: Code of Ethics, CA Act, Schedules, Council guidelines. Guidelines are reached through SS II(1).
Five principles I-O-C-C-P; five threats SSAFI; identify, evaluate, address.
First Schedule goes to the Board of Discipline: removal up to 3 months, fine up to ₹1 lakh.
Second Schedule or both goes to the Disciplinary Committee: removal for any period, fine up to ₹5 lakh.
Never share fees with a non-member, never solicit, never let a non-partner sign.
Write to the previous auditor before accepting, in writing, with proof of delivery.
Other business needs permission before you start. Substantial interest is 20%.
Contingent fees only in Regulation 192 cases.
Conviction up to 6 months: FS IV(1). Over 6 months: SS III(1).
Tax audits 60 per member, aggregate, not shareable. Company audits 30 per partner (SM).
SM figure first; one line on the 2026 Code figure.

askedAs.how: Guilty, not guilty or partly, with the clause named and each ingredient applied.
Threats and safeguards, NOCLAR, concurrent clauses, advertisement rules, networking.
Number of audits held against the limit, fee ceilings, indebtedness limits.
Facts with 3 to 5 lapses where one clause decides.
A passing line (certificate of posting, hill-area office, goodwill) becomes a full case.

pitfalls: Naming the wrong schedule: the Board of Discipline cannot give removal beyond 3 months.
Forgetting that substance beats form (an "office allowance" is still fee sharing).
Writing the 2026 Code figure as the answer instead of the SM figure.
Treating a fee dispute as a professional reason to refuse an audit.
Writing to the previous auditor after starting work.
Citing only one clause when facts engage several (for example (7), (8) and (9) together).

levels.title: How the ethics system fits together
levels.hook: Start here: which rulebook answers which question, and the three-step way to write any ethics answer.

teach.html: Code of Ethics (principles and threats), the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 (sections), the Schedules (the actual list of misconduct) and the Council Guidelines (numbers and procedures). In disciplinary cases the Schedules decide; the guidelines are reached through Second Schedule Part II Clause (1), which makes breaching any Council guideline misconduct.

The 13th edition applies from 1 April 2026 in three volumes: Vol I domestic provisions (CA Act, Schedules, Council guidelines), Vol II converged with the IESBA Code (2024 edition), Vol III Ethics Standards for Sustainability Assurance. For this exam, only the three RTP amendments change the study material (Level 11).

Provision: name the exact clause and quote its operative words. Analysis: apply each ingredient to one fact at a time, checking provisos and exceptions. Conclusion: "Hence CA X is guilty of professional misconduct under Clause (x) of Part y of the ___ Schedule." Where parts differ, give a verdict per part.

levels.correlate: Each later level maps to one slice of the Schedules. Levels 5 to 9 are the clauses; level 10 holds the guideline numbers; level 11 tells you what to write for this attempt.

recall.q: Which clause makes breach of a Council guideline misconduct?
recall.why: SS Part II Clause (1): contravening the Act, Regulations or any guidelines issued by the Council.

recall.q: Order the three steps of an ICAI ethics answer.
recall.why: Provision, analysis, conclusion.

recall.q: The Code of Ethics 2026 applies from 1 April 2026.
recall.why: The 13th edition is applicable from 1 April 2026.

recall.q: Volume III of the Code of Ethics 2026 covers…
recall.why: Vol III: Ethics Standards for Sustainability Assurance.

recall.q: Where parts of a case differ, one overall verdict is enough.
recall.why: Give a verdict per part.

twist.q: A student ends: "So he is guilty." What is missing for full conclusion marks?
twist.a: The clause. Write: "Hence CA X is guilty of professional misconduct under Clause (x) of Part y of the First/Second Schedule." Naming the clause again in the conclusion is where the mark sits.

levels.title: Fundamental principles, threats and NOCLAR
levels.hook: I-O-C-C-P and SSAFI are free marks. NOCLAR is where one line turns into a case.

teach.html: Integrity (straightforward and honest), Objectivity (no bias, conflict or undue influence), Professional competence and due care, Confidentiality (continues after the relationship ends), Professional behaviour.

Identify, evaluate (is it at an acceptable level for a reasonable and informed third party?), address (eliminate, apply safeguards, or decline). Five threats: Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation.

teach.h: When confidential information may be disclosed
teach.html: Only with proper and specific authority, or where there is a legal or professional duty or right: (a) required by law; (b) permitted by law and authorised by the client or employer; (c) a professional duty or right when not prohibited by law, such as peer or quality review, an inquiry by a regulator, protecting your own interests in legal proceedings, or complying with standards.

Non-compliance with laws and regulations by the client or employer, TCWG, management or people working for them. Steps: understand, address with management/TCWG, seek advice, determine further action, consider disclosure to an appropriate authority, imminent breach, document. India per the SM: practice (Section 360) covers audits of listed entities with net worth of ₹250 crore or more; service (Section 260) covers senior accountants in listed entities. NOCLAR goes beyond SA 250: it covers non-audit services and allows imminent-breach disclosure.

levels.correlate: Confidentiality links to Second Schedule Part I Clause (1) (practice) and Part II Clause (2) (employee) in Levels 8 and 9.

recall.q: A CA promotes his client's shares to the public. Which threat?
recall.why: Promoting a client's shares or acting as advocate for the client is an advocacy threat.

recall.q: The CA issues an assurance report on a system his own firm implemented. Which threat?
recall.why: Self-review.

recall.q: Confidentiality ends when the engagement ends.
recall.why: The duty continues after the relationship ends.

recall.q: NOCLAR in practice (SM): net worth threshold of listed entity in ₹ crore?
recall.why: Audit engagements of listed entities with net worth of ₹250 crore or more.

recall.q: Under NOCLAR the accountant must investigate the non-compliance.
recall.why: The CA is not required to investigate or ensure compliance; whether an act is non-compliance is for a court.

twist.q: A partner threatens to withhold your promotion unless you agree to an accounting treatment. Which threat, and what is the first step?
twist.a: Intimidation. Follow the framework: identify it, evaluate whether it is at an acceptable level for a reasonable and informed third party, then address it. Here that means refusing to be pressured, escalating, and if necessary ending the activity.

levels.title: CA Act sections: practice, COP, designation, branches
levels.hook: Sections 2(2), 6, 7, 8, 20, 24 to 27: many short facts, many numbers.

teach.html: A member is in practice when, for remuneration, he practises accountancy, audits or certifies financial statements, holds himself out as an accountant, or renders other prescribed services (taxation, management consultancy and other services). Offering alone is enough, even with no client.
No practice without a COP. Annual fee payable on or before 1 April; cancelled if unpaid by 30 September of the year. A suspended member cannot practise in any other capacity.

A member using "chartered accountant" may not use any other description. Not allowed on professional documents: Income-tax Consultant, Cost Accountant, Company Secretary, Management Consultant, CPA, Director, MP. Allowed: ACMA/FCMA letters, recognised foreign institutes, Insolvency Professional and Registered Valuer on cards and letterheads.
No entry on the Register if under 21 years, of unsound mind, undischarged insolvent or bankrupt, certain convictions, or removed for misconduct. Failing to disclose a disability is itself misconduct.

s.24: non-member using the designation, fine up to ₹1 lakh, then up to 6 months or ₹5 lakh. s.25: a company practising as CAs, fine ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh. s.26: a non-member signing for a CA, fine ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh. s.27 branches: each office in the charge of a member; one member may handle two offices if in the same premises, same city or within 50 km; the member must reside or attend for at least 182 days; hill-area temporary office up to 3 months.

levels.correlate: Section 26 is read with FS Part I Clause (12) (letting others sign), and section 27 breaches fall under SS Part II Clause (1).

recall.q: Minimum age to be entered on the Register (years)?
recall.why: 21 years at the time of application.

recall.q: Within how many km of the city's municipal limits can one member handle a second office?
recall.why: 50 km.

recall.q: Member in charge of a branch must reside or attend for at least…
recall.why: 182 days a year.

recall.q: A CA in practice may print "Cost Accountant" on his letterhead.
recall.why: Not allowed; ACMA/FCMA letters are allowed.

recall.q: COP annual fee unpaid by which date leads to cancellation?
recall.why: Payable by 1 April; cancelled if not paid by 30 September.

twist.q: A CA with one office in Pune opens a second office 70 km from the Pune municipal limits and puts a colleague in charge of both. Allowed?
twist.a: No — on these facts. Section 27 requires each office to be in the separate charge of a member; with a separate member in charge of each office there is no distance limit. The same premises / same city / within 50 km condition is only an exemption that lets one member be in charge of two offices. Here one colleague is put in charge of both and the second office is 70 km away, so the exemption is not available: a separate member must be put in charge of the second office.

levels.title: The disciplinary mechanism and what is misconduct
levels.hook: Board of Discipline or Disciplinary Committee? The penalty ladder decides it.

teach.html: A complaint or information goes to the Director (Discipline) for a prima facie opinion. First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline; Second Schedule or both Schedules go to the Disciplinary Committee.

Board of Discipline: reprimand; removal from the Register up to 3 months; fine up to ₹1,00,000. Disciplinary Committee: reprimand; removal permanently or for any period it thinks fit; fine up to ₹5,00,000. Appeal to the Appellate Authority within 90 days.

Professional misconduct: First Schedule Parts I, II, III and Second Schedule Parts I, II. Other misconduct: First Schedule Part IV and Second Schedule Part III, even outside professional work. Structure: FS has 12, 2, 3, 2 clauses (Parts I to IV); SS has 10, 5, 1 (Parts I to III).

levels.picture:
First ScheduleSecond Schedule
Heard byBoard of DisciplineDisciplinary Committee
RemovalUp to 3 monthsPermanent or any period
FineUp to ₹1 lakhUp to ₹5 lakh
Clauses12 + 2 + 3 + 210 + 5 + 1
levels.correlate: The Compare tab drills this table. Conviction cases split by the 6-month rule between the two Schedules (Level 9).

recall.q: Maximum fine the Board of Discipline can impose (₹ lakh)?
Maximum fine the Disciplinary Committee can impose (₹ lakh)?
A case involving both Schedules goes to…
recall.why: Second Schedule or both Schedules: Disciplinary Committee.

recall.q: Days to appeal to the Appellate Authority?
recall.why: 90 days.

recall.q: First Schedule Part IV is "professional misconduct".
recall.why: Part IV (and SS Part III) is "other misconduct".

twist.q: The Board of Discipline wants to remove a member for 6 months. Can it?
twist.a: No. The Board of Discipline can remove for up to 3 months. For a longer or permanent removal the matter must be with the Disciplinary Committee (Second Schedule or both Schedules).

levels.title: First Schedule Part I (1) to (5): sharing and securing work
levels.hook: Who may share your fees, your profits or your name, and what counts as securing work improperly.

teach.h: (1) Allowing another to practise in your name
teach.html: Allowed only if that person is also a CA in practice and is your partner or employee.

teach.h: (2) Sharing fees or profits with non-members
teach.html: You may share only with: a member of the Institute, a partner or retired partner, the legal representative of a deceased partner, a member of another professional body, or a person with prescribed qualifications. Substance over form: calling a 50% share of audit fees an "office allowance" is still sharing. A Government deduction from fees for administration is no bar.

teach.h: (3) Accepting profits of a non-member's work
teach.html: Barred, with a proviso allowing arrangements with members of other professional bodies or prescribed persons. Referral fees between members in practice are not prohibited.

Only with a CA in practice or members of prescribed professional bodies (company secretary, cost accountant, advocate, engineer, architect, actuary and recognised foreign accountancy bodies). A CA cannot be partner in an LLP that does not carry out professional work.

teach.h: (5) Securing work through non-employees or improper means
teach.html: Barred, subject to the provisos for (2), (3), (4). Canvassing through touts or letters to officials is the typical fact.

levels.correlate: (2), (3) and (4) are one family: who may share fees, profits and the practice. (5) is the net that catches everything else done through outsiders; it leads straight to soliciting in Level 6.

recall.q: A CA may pay 50% of audit fees to a non-CA as "office allowance".
recall.why: Substance over form: it is sharing of profits and is misconduct.

recall.q: May a CA in practice allow a CA who is neither partner nor employee to practise in his name?
recall.why: Only a CA in practice who is a partner or employee.

recall.q: A percentage of audit fee deducted by Government for its administrative expenses is a breach of clause (2).
recall.why: No bar: it is not sharing fees with a person.

recall.q: Which partnership is allowed?
recall.why: Advocates, cost accountants, company secretaries, engineers, architects, actuaries are allowed (Reg 53B).

recall.q: Referral fees between two members in practice are prohibited under clause (3).
recall.why: They are not prohibited.

twist.q: A CA pays his brother-in-law, a non-member who brings in clients, 10% of the audit fees received from those clients. Which clauses?
twist.a: FS Part I Clause (2) (paying a share of fees to a non-member) and Clause (5) (securing work through a person who is not an employee or partner). Name both; the first is the payment, the second is the route by which the work came.

levels.title: First Schedule Part I (6) and (7): soliciting and advertising
levels.hook: The most-tested clauses in the chapter. Learn what is permitted so you can spot what is not.

teach.html: Clause (6) asks how the CA sought work: direct or indirect solicitation is barred, whatever the medium. Clause (7) asks what the CA promotes or displays: advertising professional attainments or services, and using unauthorised descriptions on professional material, is barred. A permitted channel is not a blanket permission: apply its own conditions, and do not turn a pull channel into a push campaign.

Do not solicit clients or professional work by circular, advertisement, personal communication, interview or any other means. The provisos allow requesting work from another CA in practice and responding to user-issued tenders or enquiries. A CA-exclusive tender (such as audit or attestation) is still barred unless a minimum fee is prescribed in the tender or the area is open to other professionals. Empanelment letters may go to a known panel-maintaining body; no roving enquiries.

Bare-fact notices of a partnership change, dissolution, address or phone change are permitted, subject to the appropriate area and number of insertions. The ICAI Journal/Newsletter classified route may advertise sharing work, partnership or employment; it may include name, contact details (including website/social addresses) and factual experience/specialisation relevant to that notice. Greeting cards and invitations may carry CA and firm details only to clients, relatives and friends. Firm celebration ads are limited to Silver, Golden, Diamond, Platinum or Centenary milestones. ICAI-Council/CPE-approved CPE sponsorship is the exception to the sponsorship bar; CSR may show an individual's name with CA, never the firm name or CA logo. A CA should not take the original work of a client introduced by another member; ask the client to come through that member.

A member in practice may publish a write-up of services and firm particulars under the Council's advertisement guidelines. For the Nov 2026 exam position, the SM conditions include truthfulness; no exaggeration, disparagement or unsubstantiated comparisons; no testimonials, endorsements, client names or fees; no achievements/awards except Central/State Government or regulator awards; no positions/accreditations, monogram or catchwords; membership number/FRN mandatory; and font size not over 14. It may state permitted member/firm particulars, services and contact details. ICAI does not pre-approve it and may direct removal.

Member: name with CA, membership number, age, ACA/FCA and COP dates, recognised qualifications, languages, contact/professional address, website/email, photo, staff particulars, services and qualifying MCS-company position. Firm: firm name with Chartered Accountants, FRN, establishment year, registered office/branch addresses, working hours and contacts, partner and employee particulars/photos, services and recognised network affiliation. The allowed list is not permission to add client names, fees, testimonials, exaggerated claims or other barred matter.

A CA website is a pull model: the visitor chooses to request information. It may show permitted member/firm particulars, services, partners' qualifications/experience, staff, vacancies, articles, updates, educational videos, client-login tools and advice requested by a client. The website address may appear on professional stationery and email; a link to the firm's social page is allowed, but do not solicit visits or likes. Do not push website information by email/circular, use banner ads, or publish client names/fees except with the stated regulator-required disclosure; keep client matters confidential and information consistent with ICAI records. Telephone/trade-directory entries: under Chartered Accountants, own town, alphabetical, no differential prominence and open to all CAs of that town; trade/social directories are allowed. App aggregators listing other trades are not. A third-party advisory site is narrower: consultancy/advice only, no contact address or attainments, just that the member is a CA; no firm name with Chartered Accountants. Specialised directories/Who's Who may include the listed personal particulars, but no client names. Books/articles/presentations may state CA and firm name, not attainments. Interviews are factual answers to specific questions, not publicity; at talks/conferences, say CA only when acting as a CA and do not name the firm. TV/movie credits must not give the CA differential prominence.

On professional material, use CA and (for a qualifying firm) its name with Chartered Accountants. Recognised degrees and institute memberships, including foreign accountancy memberships recognised through an MoU/MRA, are permitted; ACMA/FCMA letters are allowed but not the words Cost Accountant. Insolvency Professional and Registered Valuer may appear on visiting cards/letterheads. Do not use descriptions such as Income-tax Consultant, Cost Accountant/Cost Consultant, Management Consultant, Company Secretary, Corporate Lawyer, CPA, Director, MP, Municipal Councillor or political-party/club office alongside CA; never use CA and Advocate/CS/CMA together when practising in that other profession. A Category IV Merchant Banker/adviser may appear in an offer document only as Advisor/Consultant to the Issue, not prominently, never as Merchant Banker, and not on own stationery. The date of setting up practice is barred on letterheads/professional documents, but may appear in a write-up or website. Personal letterhead may list all firms in which the member is a partner. The common CA India logo is allowed unchanged; firm-specific logos/monograms are not. Office boards require discretion; light only for visibility, never a trader-style glow/large board. A residence nameplate is a separate section 27 issue: individual name with CA only, not the firm's board. For coaching, no association hoardings/posters/banners; the premises signboard may show institute name, contacts and subjects.

Press notices of examination success may give the specified factual particulars (name, address, school, prize/rank, principal and firm/town) without undesirable publicity. Ads may be placed to recruit staff for the member's own office, to meet a client's staff need or business/property transaction, or for a sale handled as trustee/liquidator/receiver; do not call the firm well-known. Reports/certificates are published only to the extent needed for their purpose and on firm letterhead. Training courses may include other CAs' staff/clients but must not give the member undue prominence. In a Companies Act s.140(4) representation, be dignified, explain independent/conscientious conduct and willingness for reappointment; no publicity, canvassing or list of contributions to controls. A CA director in a prospectus/public announcement may be called Chartered Accountant and other directorships listed, but not professional attainments or firm name; ask the company to have the material approved.

Keep the exam answer distinct from later Code changes. The chapter's Nov 2026 RTP position is website pull only; the Code of Ethics 2026 permits push technology only for services not exclusive to CAs, and that change is not in the Nov 2026 RTP. For educational videos, the SM says no firm/contact/website details; the Code 2026 relaxes firm name and contact details, but not website address, and that change is likewise not in the RTP.

levels.correlate: Tenders are limited by the Council guideline (Level 10): do not respond to tenders in areas exclusively reserved for CAs unless the tender prescribes the minimum fee.

recall.q: A CA may send roving e-mails to companies likely to need an auditor.
recall.why: Roving communications are soliciting; prohibited.

recall.q: Which is allowed under clause (6)?
opts: Writing to a bank to be empanelled
E-mailing a firm profile to prospects
recall.why: Empanelment requests to panel-maintaining bodies are allowed; no roving enquiries.

recall.q: A CA website may be circulated by e-mail to prospective clients.
recall.why: Pull only: information only on a specific pull request.

recall.q: The date of setting up practice may appear on the firm's letterhead.
recall.why: It may not appear on letterheads and professional documents; it may appear in a write-up and on a website.

recall.q: Responding to a tender is allowed when…
opts: It is in an exclusively CA area with no minimum fee
The tender prescribes the minimum fee, or the area is open to other professionals too
The member asks for the fee by phone
recall.why: The Council guideline restriction does not apply where minimum fee is prescribed or the area is open to others.

recall.q: A client asks for a firm profile, which includes factual services and partner details. Which rule applies?
opts: May be supplied in response to the specific query, subject to Cl 7/write-up limits
May be sent to all similar companies
recall.why: A profile may be given after a prospective client specifically asks; write-up restrictions still apply.

recall.q: An individual CA nameplate at the member's residence is allowed if it does not name the firm.
recall.why: This is a section 27 rule: an individual nameplate with CA is allowed, not the firm's board.

twist.q: A CA e-mails his firm profile to a company that has not asked for it, "so they know us if they need an auditor". Guilty?
twist.a: Yes, under FS Part I Clause (6). A firm profile may be given to a prospective client only in response to the client's specific query. Sending it unasked is soliciting by personal communication.

levels.title: First Schedule Part I (8) to (12): the practical clauses
levels.hook: Previous auditor, 139 to 141, contingent fees, other business, signing: each has a classic fact pattern.

teach.html: Write to him before accepting. It is not a courtesy: you need to learn if there are professional reasons not to accept: non-compliance with ss.139/140; non-payment of undisputed audit fee (not for a sick unit); a qualified report by him (accept only if satisfied the qualification was not justified). Delivery needs positive evidence: registered post A/D, hand delivery against acknowledgement, registered e-mail; a certificate of posting is not enough. Writing after starting work does not cure the breach.

Check that the appointment complies with s.139 to 141 of the Companies Act, 2013 or any other law on appointment of auditors (Nov 2026 RTP wording). "Ascertain" means find out for certain; a management certificate is not enough.

Barred except under Regulation 192: receiver or liquidator (percentage of realisation), co-operative society audit, valuer for direct taxes, fund raising, debt recovery, cost optimisation, insolvency professional, and non-assurance services to non-audit clients. Fees fixed by a court are not contingent.

Barred unless Council permits. A director (not MD or whole-time) is allowed unless he or a partner is the auditor of that company. Permission must be taken before engaging. General permission covers authorship, private tutorship, honorary office, elective office and similar. Specific permission covers employment in business concerns, MD or WTD of a body corporate without substantial interest, and interests in educational institutions. Substantial interest means 20% or more. Teaching: 25 hours a week (SM).

Barred: allowing a non-member, or a member who is not your partner, to sign any balance sheet, profit and loss account, report or financial statements. Routine work may be delegated (queries, forwarding letters, initialling vouchers, memoranda of verification, acknowledgements). Delegation is no defence in an enquiry.

levels.correlate: (8) and (9) are twins at the point of taking over an audit. (12) works with s.26 of the Act; a power of attorney to sign reports also breaches SS Part II (1).

recall.q: A fee dispute is a valid professional reason to refuse the audit.
recall.why: Only non-payment of undisputed audit fee counts.

recall.q: A certificate of posting is enough proof of communication with the previous auditor.
recall.why: Positive evidence of delivery is needed.

recall.q: A contingent fee is allowed for…
opts: An audit of a listed company
recall.why: Regulation 192 allows receiver/liquidator fees as % of realisation.

recall.q: Substantial interest threshold (%)?
recall.why: 20% voting power or profits.

recall.q: Teaching hours cap per week (SM figure)?
recall.why: 25 hours a week. The Code of Ethics 2026 says 35 but the RTP does not list this change.

twist.q: A CA wrote to the outgoing auditor only after he had started the audit, and the reply raised no objection. Guilty?
twist.a: Yes under FS Part I Clause (8): he must communicate before accepting. Writing afterwards does not cure the breach, even though no objection came.

levels.title: First Schedule Parts II to IV and Second Schedule Part I
levels.hook: Employee clauses, "acting as fellow", and the ten Second Schedule clauses on duty of care.

teach.h: First Schedule Parts II and III
teach.html: Part II (member in service): (1) sharing emoluments of the employment; (2) accepting commission from a lawyer, CA or broker engaged by the employer. Part III: (1) acting as fellow without being one; (2) not supplying information to the Institute or its bodies; (3) false information while seeking work.

teach.h: Second Schedule Part I (members in practice)
teach.html: (1) Disclosing client information without consent or law. (2) Certifying without examination. (3) Vouching for forecasts. (4) Opinion where he has a substantial interest. (5) Failing to disclose a material fact. (6) Failing to report a material misstatement. (7) Lack of due diligence or gross negligence. (8) Insufficient information for an opinion. (9) Material departure from audit procedure. (10) Client money not kept in a separate account.

The duty continues after the engagement ends. Consent comes from the proprietor, any partner, or the Board of a company. Working papers belong to the auditor. Reporting fraud under s.143(12) is a legal requirement, so not a breach.

levels.correlate: Clauses (5), (6), (8) and (9) are often charged together with (7). The employee mirrors in Levels 8 and 9 (FS II(2), SS II(2)) are the same confidentiality and integrity ideas.

recall.q: A CA expresses an opinion on the financial statements of a company in which his partner has a substantial interest. Clause?
recall.why: SS Part I Clause (4).

levels.title: Second Schedule Parts II and III, and the 6-month rule
levels.hook: The gateway clause SS II(1), the new SS II(5), and the conviction split.

teach.html: (1) Contravening the Act, Regulations or Council guidelines (the gateway for every guideline). (2) Employee disclosing confidential information. (3) False particulars to the Institute. (4) Defalcation or embezzlement. (5) Acting as auditor in contravention of the Companies Act, 2013 (inserted by the 2022 amendment; listed in the Nov 2026 RTP).

Held guilty by a court for an offence punishable with imprisonment not exceeding 6 months: First Schedule Part IV(1) (Board of Discipline). Exceeding 6 months: Second Schedule Part III(1) (Disciplinary Committee). Bringing disrepute to the profession: First Schedule Part IV(2).

levels.correlate: SS II(5) works with s.141 (disqualifications), s.139 (rotation, limits) and s.144 (prohibited services). The conviction split is an example of the Board versus Committee test from Level 4.

recall.q: A CA is convicted of an offence punishable with 1 year imprisonment. Clause?
recall.why: More than 6 months: SS Part III(1), heard by the Disciplinary Committee.

recall.q: Which clause was inserted by the 2022 amendment and listed in the Nov 2026 RTP?
recall.why: SS Part II Clause (5).

recall.q: Breach of a Council guideline is covered by SS II(1).
recall.why: It is the gateway for all Council Guidelines.

recall.q: Imprisonment threshold (months) that splits FS IV(1) and SS III(1)?
recall.why: Not exceeding 6 months: FS IV(1). Exceeding: SS III(1).

recall.q: SS Part II(4) covers defalcation of moneys received in a professional capacity.
recall.why: Defalcation or embezzlement.

twist.q: A CA accepts audit of a company where he is disqualified under s.141. Which clause, and which body hears it?
twist.a: SS Part II Clause (5) (acting as auditor in contravention of the Companies Act, 2013). It is in the Second Schedule, so it goes to the Disciplinary Committee.

levels.title: Council guidelines: the numbers
levels.hook: Every guideline has a threshold. Know the SM figure and the one for 2026.

teach.html: Tax audits (RTP amendment): 60 per member per financial year, as an aggregate across individual and all firms, not shareable among partners; excludes s.44AD/44ADA/44AE audits and revised reports. Company audits (SM): 30 per member or proprietary firm; 30 per partner for firms; OPCs and dormant companies excluded; head office and its branches count as one; part-time practising partners are not counted.

Non-audit fee ceiling: for statutory audit of PSUs, Government companies, listed companies and other public companies with turnover of ₹50 crore or more, other services must not exceed the audit fee; other network firms: 3 times the audit fee. Indebtedness: ₹1,00,000 under the guideline; for companies, the Act: indebtedness above ₹5 lakh, guarantee above ₹1 lakh. Unpaid undisputed fee: do not accept; sick unit exception (registered for at least 5 years, accumulated losses equal to or more than net worth).

Tenders (7 April 2016): do not respond in areas exclusively reserved for CAs unless the minimum fee is prescribed. UDIN: certificates from 1 February 2019; GST and tax audit from 1 April 2019; all attest functions from 1 July 2019. Networking: shared profit or cost, common control, quality control, strategy, brand or significant resources. Books of account: cash book and ledger, irrespective of s.44AA.
Firms with 10 or more members should not do branch audits; for large companies encourage a firm with fewer than 5 members as joint auditor; at least 1 member for every 5 non-qualified staff.

levels.correlate: These guideline numbers are reached through SS Part II Clause (1). The 2026 Code changes several (40 audits, 35 hours, 3 years) but the RTP lists only three amendments; keep the SM figures and add one line.

twist.q: Same CA as in the base case signs 68 tax audit reports in a 4-partner firm. The firm's total is 240. Guilty?
twist.a: Yes. The limit is 60 per member, aggregate across all capacities, and cannot be distributed among partners. 68 > 60, so he is guilty by 8 reports (RTP Nov 2026, MCQ 1). SM Illustration 37's older answer no longer holds.

levels.title: What to write for this attempt: the three amendments and the 2026 Code

solves.title: Count the tax audits
solves.tip: Add every tax audit report he signed in the year across all capacities. Take out s.44AD/44ADA/44AE audits and revised reports. Then compare with 60. Never divide or share the limit between partners.

variants.label: Base case
variants.q: CA X signs, in one financial year: 12 tax audits as proprietor, 20 as partner in firm P and 25 as partner in firm Q.

steps.say: 12 + 20 + 25 = 57.
57 is not more than 60: within the limit.

variants.label: Twist 1: one more firm
variants.q: Same CA also signs 6 reports as partner in firm R.

steps.say: 57 + 6 = 63.
63 − 60 = 3.

opts: Guilty: the limit is an aggregate
steps.say: The limit is an aggregate across individual and all firms: guilty (GL: Tax audit limit).

variants.label: Twist 2: exclusions
variants.q: Of those 63 reports, 5 are audits under s.44AB for persons covered by s.44ADA, and 2 are revised reports.

steps.say: 63 − 5 − 2 = 56.
44AD/44ADA/44AE audits and revised reports are not counted. 56 is within 60.

variants.label: Twist 3: firm limit
variants.q: A 4-partner firm signs 200 tax audits in total. One partner, CA Chetan, signs 68 of them.

steps.ask: The firm's notional pooled limit if it were shareable (4 × 60).
steps.say: 4 × 60 = 240. But the limit cannot be pooled.

steps.ask: Excess of CA Chetan over his own limit.
steps.say: 68 − 60 = 8.

opts: Not guilty: the firm is within 240
steps.say: The limit is per member and cannot be shared (RTP Nov 2026, MCQ 1).

solves.title: Count the company audits
solves.tip: Ceiling = 30 × number of counted partners. Exclude OPCs and dormant companies from the count, and count a head office with its branches as one. Part-time practising partners are not counted.

variants.label: Base case
variants.q: A firm has 3 partners, one of whom is a part-time practising partner. It holds 68 company audits, including 5 One Person Companies and 3 dormant companies. SM figure: 30 per partner.

steps.say: 3 − 1 part-time = 2.
2 × 30 = 60.

steps.ask: Company audits counted (exclude OPCs and dormant).
steps.say: 68 − 5 − 3 = 60.

steps.ask: Can it accept one more company audit?
steps.say: It is at the ceiling of 60; one more makes 61.

variants.label: Twist 1: new partner
variants.q: On the date of acceptance of a new audit, a third full-time partner has joined (so 3 counted partners).

steps.say: 3 × 30 = 90.
The number of partners on the date of acceptance counts.

solves.title: Non-audit fee ceiling
solves.tip: Add the other fees of the auditor and of his associate concerns, then compare with the statutory audit fee. Leave out other statutory audits, certification the auditor must do, and representation before an authority.

variants.label: Base case
variants.q: A CA is statutory auditor of a listed company (turnover well above ₹50 crore), fee ₹20 lakh. He also earns ₹12 lakh for other services, and his associate concern earns ₹6 lakh from the company.

steps.say: 12 + 6 = 18.
18 is not more than 20: within.

variants.label: Twist 1: associate bills more
variants.q: Same, but the associate concern earns ₹10 lakh.

steps.say: 12 + 10 = 22.

opts: Exceeds: he should not have accepted the appointment
steps.say: 22 exceeds 20. The limit applies to the auditor and his associate concerns together.

variants.label: Twist 2: exclusions
variants.q: Same as twist 1, but ₹4 lakh of the auditor's ₹12 lakh is certification work required to be done by the statutory auditor.

steps.ask: Fee counted against the ceiling (₹ lakh).
steps.say: (12 − 4) + 10 = 18. Certification required of the statutory auditor is not "other work".
18 is within 20.

variants.label: Twist 3: small public company
variants.q: Same fees as twist 1, but the company is an unlisted public company with turnover of ₹40 crore.

opts: No: turnover is below ₹50 crore and it is not a PSU, Government or listed company
steps.say: The ceiling applies to PSUs, Government companies, listed companies and other public companies with turnover of ₹50 crore or more.

variants.label: Twist 4: network firms
variants.q: Statutory audit fee ₹20 lakh. Other firms of the auditor's network earn ₹55 lakh from the company in total for other services.

steps.ask: Network ceiling: 3 times the audit fee (₹ lakh).
steps.say: 3 × 20 = 60.
55 is within 60.

solves.title: Indebtedness limits
solves.tip: Decide first: is the concern a company? For a company use the Act (indebtedness above ₹5 lakh; guarantee above ₹1 lakh). For any other concern the guideline figure is above ₹1,00,000.

variants.label: Base case
variants.q: A CA owes a company ₹4 lakh. Can he accept its audit?

steps.ask: Statutory indebtedness threshold for a company (₹ lakh).
steps.say: s.141(3)(d)(ii): indebtedness above ₹5 lakh disqualifies. Threshold ₹5 lakh.

opts: Yes: ₹4 lakh does not exceed ₹5 lakh
steps.say: ₹4 lakh is within the statutory limit.

variants.label: Twist 1: guarantee
variants.q: The CA gave a guarantee of ₹1.5 lakh for a third person's debt to the company.

steps.say: s.141(3)(d)(iii): guarantee or security above ₹1 lakh. Threshold ₹1 lakh.
₹1.5 lakh exceeds ₹1 lakh: disqualified.

variants.label: Twist 2: not a company
variants.q: The CA owes ₹1.5 lakh to a partnership firm whose audit he is offered (not a company).

opts: The s.141 company limit of ₹5 lakh
steps.say: For concerns other than companies the Council guideline applies: above ₹1,00,000.
₹1.5 lakh exceeds ₹1,00,000.

solves.title: Unpaid fee and the sick-unit exception
solves.tip: Test two things for sickness: registered for at least 5 years, and accumulated losses at least equal to net worth. Both must hold.

variants.label: Base case
variants.q: The previous auditor's undisputed fee is unpaid. The company has been registered for 6 years, with net worth ₹10 crore and accumulated losses ₹12 crore.

steps.say: 6 years is at least 5.

steps.ask: Accumulated losses at least equal to net worth?
steps.say: ₹12 crore is not less than ₹10 crore.
It is a sick unit, so the unpaid-fee bar does not apply.

variants.label: Twist: young company
variants.q: Same numbers, but the company was registered 4 years ago.

steps.say: The 5-year test fails, even though losses exceed net worth.
Not a sick unit, so accepting would breach the guideline.

hooks.h: Two Schedules: house rules and criminal law
hooks.story: The First Schedule is the house rules of the profession (how you win work, whom you share with, what you may display). A breach is dealt with by the Board of Discipline with modest penalties. The Second Schedule is about duty of care (what you owe the client and the public). A breach is dealt with by the Disciplinary Committee, which can remove you permanently.

The examiner reads facts like a judge reads a contract: a label does not change what the act is. An "office allowance" to a non-CA that equals half the audit fee is fee sharing. A "management certificate" is not "ascertaining" compliance. A "limit shared among partners" is not 60 per member.

links.how: First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline: removal up to 3 months, fine up to ₹1 lakh.
Removal for any period, fine up to ₹5 lakh.

links.a: FS Part IV(1): up to 6 months
links.how: The conviction split decides the Schedule and therefore the forum.
(6) is asking for work; (7) is advertising your attainments or using other designations.
(2) is paying a share out to a non-member; (3) is taking a part of a non-member's profits.
Both are checks you do before accepting an audit; (9) is a Nov 2026 RTP wording change.
Read together: a non-member signing for a CA in practice is an offence under s.26.
Breach of a Council guideline is misconduct through SS Part II Clause (1).
Acting as auditor in contravention of the Act; works with rotation, disqualification and prohibited services.
SS I(1) for practice; SS II(2) for an employee. Same principle, different clause.
FS III(2) is silence or non-compliance; SS II(3) is knowingly false information.
Often charged together (and with (9)) on the same facts.
60 per member, aggregate and not shareable (RTP amendment); 30 per partner (SM figure, 40 in the 2026 Code).
Not applicable to a sick unit: registered at least 5 years and losses at or above net worth.
Contingent or percentage fees are barred except in the Regulation 192 cases.
Responding to tenders is allowed under the proviso, but the guideline limits it in areas exclusive to CAs.
A UDIN-based communication is recognised as evidence of communication.
SA 250 is audit only; NOCLAR also covers non-audit services and allows imminent-breach disclosure.

links.b: Other AAA chapters on independence and audit quality
links.how: Substantial interest and the 20% test recur wherever auditor independence is tested.
